title: [storage] releasing a scratch folder that is already gone is no error (it prints {"gone":"<dir>"}), and a kept scratch reading leaves out a claimed folder removed since
prompt:
Spawn, objective 220 [storage] (the lead 14:2x as 218, scope YES as 220 since rev-i holds 218; changes 1 and 2 both in; author rev-j; readers rev-g first, rev-i second): `spawn scratch release` accepts a folder that is gone, and the storage line's kept reading stops listing a claimed folder removed since.

Why. 140's claim lives in the folder's owner file (.spawn-owner). An agent that removes its folder whole (rm -rf, the usual end of a round) and then releases it, as 140's rules ask, gets "No such file or directory" and exit 1 (the lead after a landing, 2026-11-18). The claim is gone already, since the file went with the folder, but the agent's script sees a failure and the release step reads as undone. One place keeps a removed folder's claim on view: the storage line's reading. When a scratch walk runs over its bound, unowned.rs keeps the previous reading's figure and its claimed folders whole (`previous.claimed.clone()`), so a folder removed since is listed as claimed, with its owner and lease, until a walk fits its bound again (live 2026-11-18: 34 claimed folders, all present; this is the case of a bound overrun, as /data/tmp's before 155).

What changes (crates/spawn-cli only):
1. scratch_owner.rs: `spawn scratch release <dir>` on a folder that is gone prints `{"gone":"<dir>"}` and exits 0, writing nothing. Gone means: the name is absolute with no `.`/`..` part, and walking it from / every part that exists is a real directory (lstat, never followed), until one part does not exist (NotFound). Any other name goes on to release as before, so these are still refused (exit 1): a relative name, a name with `..`, a missing folder under a symlink or under a file, an existing folder with no claim, or any other error than NotFound on the way. `renew` of a gone folder is refused as before (a lease cannot run on nothing). A folder still there releases as before (its claim's line, lease_until_ms = now).
2. unowned.rs: a walk past its bound keeps the previous figure and the previous claimed folders, but those no longer a real directory (lstat: removed, or now a symlink or a file) are left out (`still_there`). Nothing else of the kept reading changes; a walk within its bound is as before.
The module docs say both.

Never changed: 140's owner file and its fields, claim, renew, the sweep (145), the walk's rules (155), what a fitting walk lists, read only in serve, no symlink followed.

Tests (unit): scratch_owner/tests.rs a_release_finds_a_removed_folder_gone_and_nothing_else (a removed claimed folder and one whose parent is removed are gone; relative, `..`, an existing folder, under a symlink, under a file are not; renew of the gone folder fails with No such file); unowned.rs a_kept_reading_leaves_out_a_claimed_folder_removed_since (a walk over a 3-entry bound keeps the previous figure, and of claimed [here, removed, a symlink] lists here only).

Files: crates/spawn-cli/src/scratch_owner.rs, crates/spawn-cli/src/scratch_owner/tests.rs, crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines/unowned.rs. Owner: rsi/scenarios/220.sh, rsi/backlog/220.json.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/220.sh, black box, its own database, a scratch HOME, `spawn scratch` and `spawn serve` on 127.0.0.1:0:
(1) claim S/g, rm -rf it, release S/g: exit 0, stdout exactly {"gone":"S/g"}, S/g not made;
(2) the same with the parent S/p removed, for S/p/q;
(3) refused, exit 1 with no "gone", the scratch unchanged: a relative name, a name with .., a missing folder under a symlink, a missing folder under a file, a missing folder under a directory that cannot be searched (permission denied; skipped as root), an existing folder with no claim, renew of a removed folder;
(4) a claimed folder still there releases: exit 0, its line (agent, objective), lease_until_ms at most now, its owner file kept;
(5) serve with scratch_bound 100000 entries over a root with claimed G, K and L and an idle folder of 30 files: claimed lists G, K and L; G removed, L replaced by a symlink to K, and the bound set to 3 (a new plan, so a new reading that runs over its bound and keeps the previous one): once the log says "ran over its bound (3 entries", claimed lists K only.
On live main the scenario exits 1: (1), (2) exit 1 with No such file, and (5) lists G.

Verified by: the next agent that removes a claimed folder and then releases it gets {"gone":...} and exit 0 (the lead's or the agent's own word), and the Home card's Storage row lists no claimed folder that is gone.
